reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the role of magnetic interactions and frustration in fcc–hcp phase stability for CrCoNi and Mn-containing ternaries, but it does not address Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni. The extrapolation to the quinary alloy, the specific role of Cr ordering in that system, and the predicted mechanical property enhancements are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Magnetic interactions, especially Cr ordering, govern fcc–hcp phase stability in CrCoNi-based alloys.
Magnetic frustration (e.g., from Mn) eliminates the fcc–hcp energy difference and suppresses the transformation.
Reducing magnetic frustration in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni will lower stacking fault energy and promote fcc-to-hcp transformation.
The fcc-to-hcp transformation generates a nano-dual-phase structure that enhances cryogenic toughness and strain hardening.
The proposed mechanism applies to Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni because it contains Cr and lacks strongly frustrated elements like Mn.
